newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to complete sell-off process by mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to complete sell-off process by mid-1997.

text.p: Slovenia's Privatisation Agency said on Monday the country's mass privatisation scheme should be completed by mid-1997, three and a half years after its inception.
"The privatisation of the remaining companies is just a technical question," Mira Puc, the agency's director, told a news conference.
"By the end of November, 800 companies had completed their privatisation, while another 1029 were still in the process," deputy agency director Joze Jaklin said.
About 10 percent of all the country's enterprises have not yet entered the scheme following revisions in the evaluation of large state companies and their units.

Under Slovenia's massive sell-off scheme, kicked off in the beginning of 1994, every Slovene received a voucher whose value varied according to age, ranging from 100,000 tolars ($719) for people under 18 to 400,000 tolars for people over 48.
More than 88 percent of Slovenians have spent their privatisation vouchers until now by placing them with Slovenian investment funds or buying shares directly.
"Slovenia probably has the highest percentage of spent vouchers among the countries that recently have went through similar processes," Puc said.

In September, the Slovenian government decided to prolong the validity of privatisation vouchers for the fourth time in a row, extending them to the end of June 1997. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
